item.title: New coordinator role enhances support for medical first responders in PEI
item.description:
New coordinator role enhances support for medical first responders in PEI jenniferdhogan Fri, 10/30/2026 - 13:10

Kenneth Ramsay knows firsthand what it’s like to be the first person to arrive at an emergency scene.

Ramsay has helped Islanders through some of the most difficult moments of their lives. Whether stopping a severe bleed or providing lifesaving breaths, he has spent 21 years as a paramedic and 27 years as a volunteer firefighter serving his community. 

Now, Ramsay is bringing that experience to his new role as coordinator of the Medical First Responder (MFR) Program, a partnership between Island EMS, PEI Firefighters Association and the provincial government. The program ensures firefighters have the training they need to provide emergency medical care to people before paramedics reach the scene. 

“I have a personal interest in the program,” Ramsay said. “Over the years, while teaching firefighters to become medical first responders, I saw a lot of opportunities for growth in the program. I felt this was something I could make a difference in because I understand the program.”

Since starting this position in the spring, Ramsay has focused on building a strong foundation for the program. He is working with partners to establish an advisory committee, developing a new website, and supporting fire departments with day-to-day needs such as program resources and medical supplies, including AED pads, oxygen and trauma dressings. 

His goal is to create greater consistency across the province and ensure fire departments are aligned with Island EMS clinical practice guidelines.

“Right now, fire departments each have their own approaches and processes,” Ramsay said. “I would like to see it standardized, bring everyone on the same page, and make the whole emergency health system work better.”

PEI currently has 35 fire departments and hundreds of trained medical first responders who play a vital role in emergency response, particularly in rural communities where they are often among the first to arrive and begin patient care.

“Often, they’re on scene before the ambulance arrives and providing lifesaving care,” Ramsay said. “I’ve witnessed many instances where medical first responders have brought people back to life from cardiac arrest before paramedics arrived.”

When asked what message he would like Islanders to know about firefighters who serve as medical first responders, Ramsay’s answer is simple. 

“I want Islanders to know we will always be there for you. We will provide care to the best of our ability, and we will do so with compassion.”

Next steps include establishing the advisory committee and holding its first meeting before the end of the year to help guide the future direction of the program.   

“The goal is to create a more integrated medical first responder program that strengthens coordination between MFRs and Island EMS,” Ramsay said.

The coordinator position is funded by the provincial government as part of its investments to strengthen the MFR Program.

item.title: New resources available for farm succession planning on Prince Edward Island
item.description:
New resources available for farm succession planning on Prince Edward Island ddgillis Fri, 10/30/2026 - 11:15

Farmers preparing for ownership transition can access new resources to help them plan for passing on their farm business. 

The Step Toward the Future hub brings information and resources together in one place to help farmers think ahead, seek advice, and work through the decisions involved in succession. Producers can visit the hub to find upcoming workshops, access a free online succession-preparation course, and explore new planning tools and resources as they are added.

“Succession planning is vital for the continued sustainability and economic growth of our farming industry on Prince Edward Island,” said the Honourable Heath MacDonald, Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food. “With many producers retiring in the years ahead, this new hub will provide the information and resources to help new and aspiring farmers step into the industry with confidence and success.”

“Supporting the next generation of farmers continues to be a priority for Prince Edward Island. A strong future for Island agriculture depends on great planning today, and this succession planning hub will be a valuable resource as people prepare for the future of their farms.”

- Agriculture Minister Hilton MacLennan.

Succession isn’t just the transfer of tasks, skills, or assets; it is also the transfer of leadership. Succession planning ensures a smooth transition from an outgoing farmer or older generation to the next generation. More than 40 per cent of Canadian farm operators will retire in the next decade. On Prince Edward Island, only 10.5 per cent of farmers have a written succession plan, according to the 2021 census. The Step Toward the Future hub provides farmers with a clear path forward to support generational farming on Prince Edward Island. 

There will also be a series of information sessions this fall and next year to help guide farmers in their planning. 

The first Next Generation Farm Succession Workshop will take place on November 28 and will feature Patti Durand, a certified Family Enterprise Advisor who has guided hundreds of Canadian farm business families through transition planning and decision making.

“In 2024, PEI’s agriculture and agri-food exports reached $1.05 billion, the highest in the province’s history,” said Minister MacLennan. “With thoughtful succession planning, that growth can continue, farmers can stay confident, and the next generation can be set up for success.”

Producers are encouraged to check the Step Toward the Future hub regularly for updates on workshops, a succession planning guidebook, supplementary tools, and other resources.

The Step Toward the Future hub is funded in part by the Sustainable Canadian Agricultural Partnership, 5-year, $3.5-billion investment by federal, provincial and territorial governments to strengthen competitiveness, innovation, and resiliency of Canada’s agriculture, agri‐food, and agri‐based products sector. This includes $1 billion in federal programs and activities and a $2.5-billion commitment that is cost-shared 60 per cent federally and 40 per cent provincially/territorially for programs that are designed and delivered by provinces and territories.
